comparator.name: International Business Administration
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted 2026–2027 schedule has 60 EC in each year. Year one has ten compulsory courses. Year two has eight compulsory courses and two 6 EC electives, one in each of periods 4 and 5. The selected electives are Accounting, Business and Society and Corporate Finance: A Sustainability Perspective. Year three contains a 30 EC exchange, 6 EC Ethics, two 6 EC Strategy and Organization courses, and the 12 EC individual thesis. The adopted OER ties the English diagnostic test or refresher to Academic Skills. A public Study Guide description instead names Global Sustainability for this cohort. This example follows the adopted rule and completes the requirement before either grade. Research Participation I and II are zero-credit requirements for receiving Business Processes and Integrative Research Project credits, respectively. Quantitative Business Research Methods requires Business Mathematics. Exchange normally requires 60 EC at application, a completed first year and 90 EC before departure, and approval of the planned courses. The illustrated route completes years one and two before exchange. The thesis requires Academic Skills and both Business Research Methods courses, registration and supervisor selection. Students undertake supervised individual research in the chosen specialisation.

courses: Business & Economy in the Age of AI

core: International business administration: how firms are organised, managed and operated across borders
Cross-cultural management: how culture and values shape business behaviour, consumer response and management decisions
Global economics: micro- and macroeconomic principles applied to an integrated world economy
Accounting, corporate finance and financial decision-making
Quantitative and qualitative business research methods, statistics and an integrative empirical research project
People in business and society: organisational behaviour, leadership and the management of diverse teams
International strategy, digital technologies and the responsible use of AI in business
Global supply chains, international trade and the cross-border operating environment
Ethics, corporate social responsibility and sustainability in global business
adjacent: Responsible and sustainable international business: sustainability science, circular production and the governance of sustainability
Consumer behaviour and consumer psychology as the basis of marketing decisions
The societal and cultural context in which firms and markets operate
Public policy, regulation and the political economy of international business
questions: How can a company introduce a product and build consumer trust in an unfamiliar cultural market?
How do different cultures view corporate social responsibility and responsible finance, and how should an international firm act on that?
How can trust and cooperation be built in culturally diverse and virtual international teams?
How do European, Asian and South American business environments differ, and what does that mean for strategy and supply chains?
How should persuasion, branding and marketing communication be used responsibly across cultures?

trace: Experiential venture development, market validation and business planning give substantive enterprise decision-making practice; not the same manufacturing-process bootcamp as VU BusinessProcesses.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target is the generic International Business Administration bachelor, and the adopted 2026-2027 programme schedule requires one of eleven year-3 specializations, each fixing two 6-EC courses and the subject of the 12-EC thesis, so one must be instantiated. The regulations define the programme as international business administration and state that it prepares students for a subsequent master's in Business Administration or Entrepreneurship; its compulsory core includes Organization Theory, International Strategy and Business Processes. Accounting, Economics, Finance, Financial Management, Marketing, Strategic Human Resource Management / Leadership and Change Management, Digital Business Innovation and Transport and Supply Chain Management each deepen one functional discipline, while Entrepreneurship and Management Consulting apply strategy to a particular setting. Strategy and Organization is the general-management specialization of business administration: both of its courses list the compulsory Organization Theory and International Strategy courses as recommended background, and Foundations of Strategic Management is also the shared first course of the Entrepreneurship and Management Consulting specializations. It therefore best represents the programme's broad business-administration identity. The choice was made from the official evidence alone and does not improve the UCR match: both specialization rows and the thesis remain without a UCR counterpart.

selection.assessment: The first option gives broad management, markets and finance the greatest weight. The second focuses on business responsibility through life-cycle analysis, climate, public economics, policy methods and governance. The third focuses on consumer behaviour, design, marketing research and persuasive communication. All three sustain substantial business study. Their differences concern the questions and methods students study. Operations and supply chains, enterprise information systems, mandatory exchange and the VU specialisation thesis remain distinct.

blocks: Academic foundations, research methods and independent research
Both develop academic writing and source evaluation. UCR also includes personal and civic development.
Both teach descriptive and inferential statistics. UCR combines them with research design and a project.
Both develop statistical analysis for empirical research. UCR uses health and behavioural examples.
Both teach qualitative research design and interpretation. UCR applies these methods to social research.
Both integrate research design, evidence collection, analysis and reporting. UCR applies these methods to market research.
VU requires a dedicated business mathematics course.
VU requires a 12 EC individual thesis in the chosen specialisation. UCR’s optional independent research sits outside the scheduled 180 EC.
Firms, organisations and the people in them
Both study behaviour relevant to managing people. UCR focuses on leadership, individual differences and performance under pressure.
Both study how organisations work. UCR concentrates on organisational behaviour and leadership.
VU requires study of the design and management of business processes.
VU introduces people and organisations in their societal and business settings.
Both introduce market behaviour and macroeconomic principles. VU frames them around the global economy.
Both teach accounting and financial statement analysis.
Both study finance and risk. UCR places more weight on financial systems, banking and monetary policy.
Strategy, markets, consumers and the international business environment
Both develop strategic analysis. UCR focuses on digital change, while VU emphasises international strategy.
Both develop marketing and consumer analysis. VU focuses on marketing across cultures, while UCR includes branding and digital engagement.
VU covers global supply chains, including sourcing, logistics and operations.
Both introduce sustainability. UCR approaches it through sustainability science, while VU applies it to business.
Both teach ethical reasoning. UCR applies it to broader questions such as inequality, climate and obligations to future generations.
Digital technology, data and AI in business
VU studies how businesses design and use information systems.
Electives, specialization and exchange in the external programme
This VU elective studies reporting, carbon accounting, budgeting and control.
This VU elective studies valuation, financing and sustainability in corporate finance.
VU develops advanced strategic management in the selected specialisation.
VU applies strategic management through decisions and planning from a chief executive’s perspective.
VU requires an approved 30 EC exchange semester.

notes.text: The UCR options share business foundations and differ in emphasis. VU adds dedicated operations and supply-chain management, business information systems, an exchange and a supervised specialisation thesis. UCR’s optional independent research is separate from the scheduled degree.
VU combines compulsory courses, restricted electives, exchange and a specialisation. Each UCR option combines 24 courses across six semesters.

audience.programmeDescription: VU International Business Administration studies how firms operate across borders and cultures. Students develop knowledge of management, economics, marketing, accounting and finance, research methods, sustainability and responsible digital business, then complete an exchange, a specialisation and an individual thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The first UCR option focuses on management, markets and finance. The second uses environmental and policy courses to study business responsibility. The third combines consumer behaviour, product development and communication. VU adds specialist operations and information systems, a required exchange and a supervised thesis.
